title: AssayStandard
description: The measured, versioned reliability of a verifier ('judge') — the calibrated reference every ReasoningAssay is checked against. Answers 'who verifies the verifier' mechanically: a verdict may only claim 'ok' when it points at a standard whose reliability was actually measured. Re-measuring publishes a new version; historical assays that reference an older version can be re-projected against the newer one.

id.description: Stable URN for this measured standard. Pattern: urn:srcos:assay-standard:<verifier-slug>:<version>.

verifierId.description: URN or stable identifier of the verifier/judge whose reliability this standard records.

version.description: Version of the verifier at the time of measurement. A new measurement of the same verifier yields a new AssayStandard with a bumped version.

confusionMatrix.description: Raw counts from the calibration run. Facts, not interpretation — metrics below are derived from these and may be recomputed.

metrics.description: Optional derived scores (recomputable from confusionMatrix). Present as a convenience; the matrix is authoritative.

interRaterAgreement.description: Optional inter-rater reliability when the standard was set against multiple human/reference judges.

sampleSize.description: Number of labelled items the standard was measured over. A standard measured on too few items is itself weak evidence.

calibrated.description: Whether this standard clears the project's minimum bar to let a referencing assay project to 'ok'. Uncalibrated standards can still be recorded — a referencing assay then projects no better than 'sad'.

measuredAt.description: When the measurement was taken. Standards are perishable; consumers may treat an old measurement as stale.
